name: Battle of Poltava

phases.title: The Swedes form south of the redoubts
phases.text: The Swedish columns formed in the night 600 metres south of the redoubts, with the Russian cavalry behind the redoubts and the camp beyond. The infantry was in place early, but the cavalry arrived late.

phases.title: The Swedish wings pass the redoubts
phases.text: Roos' column overran the first two redoubts but stalled at the third. Lewenhaupt's battalions on the right and Hamilton's cavalry on the left went past the redoubts, and the Russian cavalry retreated.

phases.title: Lewenhaupt withdraws west and Roos is cut off
phases.text: Rehnskiöld stopped the pursuit and ordered Lewenhaupt to withdraw to the west, where the wings waited for Roos' battalions. Roos led his remaining 1,500 men into the Yakovetski woods to the east.

phases.title: Roos is driven back and surrenders
phases.text: The Russians retook the first two redoubts and attacked Roos with ten regiments. He fell back towards Poltava, took refuge in an abandoned fort and surrendered at 9:30 a.m.

phases.title: Peter advances and the Swedish line moves forward
phases.text: Peter led his infantry out of the camp, with dragoons on his right and Menshikov's cavalry on his left. Rehnskiöld ordered Lewenhaupt and the Swedish line forward, and the Russian first line retreated towards its second line.

phases.title: The Swedish left flank breaks
phases.text: The Russian line was longer, and the Swedish infantry on the left flank threw down their weapons and fled. A gap opened in the Swedish line, the Russians filled it, and Menshikov's cavalry attacked the Swedes from the rear.

phases.title: The Swedish assault disintegrates
phases.text: Small groups of Swedes broke through and escaped to the south through the Budyschenski woods, while many of the rest were overwhelmed, ridden down or captured. Charles ordered a retreat to the woods with what forces he could gather.

note: North is drawn at the top because the Russian camp lay north of Poltava and the Yakovetski woods lay to the east of the Swedish attack. The accounts do not say exactly where either wood lay, so the Budyschenski wood is placed to the south-west, where the Swedes escaped, and the Yakovetski wood to the east. The ten redoubts are drawn as one block. The plan moves the fighting west of the Russian camp as the accounts say, but the distances are not to scale. The accounts give the date in the Gregorian calendar as 8 July 1709 and the hours by the Swedish calendar.
